newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian LOMO breaks even in 1996.
newsitem.headline: Russian LOMO breaks even in 1996.

text.p: Russia optical goods company AO Leningradskoye Optiko-Mekhanicheskoye Obyedineniye (LOMO) broke even in 1996 as it has switched to a new accounting system, a company spokesman said on Tuesday.

"According to our 1996 production volumes there was a 10 billion rouble profit, but according to new rules overdue debtor debts must be transferred to the company's expenditure and there were losses which were covered from the reserve fund and other sources," Lazar Zalmanov told Reuters.
He also said there was a fall in orders from the public sector compared with 1995.
"Due to a fall in orders we have received about 50 billion roubles less from the Central Election Commission and 25 billion roubles less from the Defence Ministry," Zalmanov said.
The Central Election Commission ordered scanners from LOMO in 1995 to count votes in elections at the end of the year and in mid-1996.
LOMO's supervisory board decided recently not to pay 1996 dividends and to consider paying dividends on preferred shares for the first quarter of 1997, he said.
Sales volume 186.0 bln rbls 146.0 bln rbls
NOTE - A share face value is 5,000 roubles. The company specialises in optic and electronic machinery.
